title: BSOD triggered when AlwaysOnTop module is enabled, especially around display sleep/reconfiguration

judgment.rationale: The report is credible and high impact, but focused public code review cannot establish the exact PowerToys call path behind the win32k recursion.
evidence: Three matching 0x7F/8 win32k recursion signatures are reported.
Disabling Always On Top stopped recurrence in the described scenarios.
AlwaysOnTop.cpp owns WinEvent hooks, tracked topmost windows, and WindowBorder instances.
The latest timeline includes a new report ZIP and a Needs-Team-Response label.
No confirmed fix or duplicate was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a readable current diagnostic correlation before approving a kernel-sensitive fix design.

fix_assessment.rationale: A confirmed PowerToys fix is not yet applicable because the failing call path is unproven; the next action is targeted evidence collection.

issue_context.summary: The reporter supplied three matching 0x7F double-fault signatures during repeated display power/reconfiguration events and says disabling Always On Top stopped the crashes. Public source shows WinEvent hooks, topmost-window tracking, and border windows, but does not prove which interaction reaches the win32k recursion.
known_information: Issue is open with Product-Always On Top and Needs-Team-Response.
The report describes sleep, monitor power-cycle, and lock/display-timeout triggers.
The report identifies recursive win32kbase PDEV dereferencing.
A new report ZIP was attached on 2026-09-03 after the earlier archive was rejected.
AlwaysOnTop.cpp subscribes to location/move/foreground/destroy events and tracks WindowBorder instances.
inferences: Always On Top may provoke a win32k teardown/reconfiguration race through tracked windows or borders, but the exact failing call path is unconfirmed.
A code fix should not be designed from the bugcheck signature alone.
issue_context.analysis: The evidence is strong at symptom level, yet the focused source/history review cannot identify a confirmed PowerToys root cause. Request targeted dump/report correlation before a kernel-sensitive design.
initial_investigation: Inspected AlwaysOnTop.cpp WinEvent subscriptions, tracked windows, and WindowBorder ownership.
Read the full timeline and noted the new ZIP and team-response label.
Found no existing upstream fix PR or confirmed duplicate.

information_gaps.information: Readable crash dump/report correlating the active Always On Top state and owned border/topmost windows at failure
information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguishes a PowerToys operation from a display-driver/window-manager fault
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce on latest stable and submit a fresh /bugreport immediately after the next occurrence, retaining the matching dump if available

actions.label: Request Always On Top crash correlation

comment.body: The report gives three matching 0x7F/8 win32k recursion signatures and says disabling Always On Top stopped recurrence. Focused source review confirms that Always On Top owns WinEvent hooks and WindowBorder tracking, but not which operation reaches the failing kernel path. Please reproduce on the latest stable release and submit a fresh /bugreport immediately after the next occurrence, retaining the matching dump if available. The needed evidence is crash-time Always On Top/module state and stack correlation, not a generic log bundle.
